source_evidence.observation: The paper defines matrix absolute value componentwise as |A|=(|a_ij|). Consequently, the factor |x|^T|y| used later is the scalar sum of the absolute products, not a norm. [PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: componentwise absolute-value convention]

The standard model is fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta), equivalently fl(a op b)=(a op b)/(1+delta), with |delta|<=u for op in {+,-,multiplication,division}. The paper defines gamma_k=ku/(1-ku), assumes ku<1 for every relevant k and precision, and transfers accents and FMA superscripts from gamma to its underlying unit roundoff. [PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.4) and gamma notation]

The general block-FMA model computes C+AB internally at precision bar_u and returns at precision u_FMA, where u_FMA is u_low or u_high. Its matrix bound is |hat_D-D|<=u_FMA|hat_D|+bar_gamma_(b+1)(|C|+|A||B|). Setting bar_u=0 represents the rounded-exact extreme only up to O(u_FMA^2), because hat_D rather than D occurs on the right. [PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.5)-(2.6) and block-FMA precision model]

Algorithm 3.1 multiplies A in R^{m x n} and B in R^{n x t}, partitioned into b1 x b and b x b2 blocks, with integer p=m/b1, q=n/b, and r=t/b2. It converts A and B to u_low if necessary, initializes each output block to zero, chains q block FMAs with output precision u_FMA, and rounds the completed block to output precision u when u differs from u_FMA. [PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1]

The inputs need not originally be in u_low, and scaling may be needed in practice, but the analysis explicitly assumes that underflow and overflow do not occur. [PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1]

For a row x of A and column y of B, the exact dot product s_n=x^T y is divided into q=n/b consecutive blocks of b products. The block recurrence starts at s_0=0 and forms s_i=s_(i-1)+x_((i-1)b+1)y_((i-1)b+1)+...+x_(ib)y_(ib) for i=1:q. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1)]

Under left-to-right internal evaluation, each computed block result has indexed theta and delta factors. The effective output-rounding unit tilde_u_FMA is selected with priority: u if u>u_FMA; otherwise 0 if bar_u>=u_FMA; otherwise u_FMA if bar_u<u_FMA. The paper explicitly says the first case takes precedence when conditions overlap. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.2)-(3.3)]

The unrolled computation has the exact factorized representation hat_s_n=sum_(k=1)^n x_k y_k(1+alpha_k)(1+beta_k), with |alpha_k|<=tilde_gamma_q^FMA and |beta_k|<=bar_gamma_n. It therefore satisfies |s_n-hat_s_n|<=(tilde_gamma_q^FMA+bar_gamma_n+tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n)|x|^T|y|. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: compact factorization and equation (3.4)]

For right-to-left evaluation, identified as blocked summation, every occurrence of bar_gamma_n in (3.4) may be replaced by bar_gamma_(q+b-1). The paper additionally states that the original bound (3.4) is valid for all orders of evaluation of (3.1). [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.4)]

binders: Choose positive integer dimensions m,n,t and block dimensions b1,b,b2 for which p=m/b1, q=n/b, and r=t/b2 are integers; the local result uses q=n/b and hence qb=n. [PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1)]

For any selected row x of A and column y of B, both having n components, let s_n=x^T y denote their exact dot product and let hat_s_n denote the corresponding computed chained-block result. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1) and equation (3.4)]

Let bar_u denote the unit roundoff of the internal block-FMA evaluation, u_FMA the block-FMA output unit roundoff, and u the requested output unit roundoff. [PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: block-FMA precision model; PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.1)-(3.3)]

After the dimensions, operands, precisions, and computation are fixed, the analysis supplies per-block witnesses theta_j^(i) and delta_i, followed by per-product witnesses alpha_k and beta_k for k=1,...,n. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.2) and compact factorization preceding equation (3.4)]
hypotheses: The dot-product length is exactly divisible by the block width: q=n/b is an integer and qb=n. [PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1)]
The exact dot product is grouped into q consecutive blocks, and the computed accumulation starts from zero using the recurrence in (3.1). [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1)]

For the displayed derivation of (3.2), each recurrence right-hand side is evaluated internally at precision bar_u from left to right and then subjected to the modeled output rounding. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: text between equations (3.1) and (3.2)]

Every elementary operation obeys the standard relative-error model, and every decorated gamma constant is defined only under the inherited condition that its index times its corresponding unit roundoff is less than one. [PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.4) and gamma notation]
When u>u_FMA>bar_u would physically require two roundings, the analysis deliberately models only one rounding. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: text between equations (3.1) and (3.2)]

conclusions: For each i=1,...,q, the computed value satisfies hat_s_i=[hat_s_(i-1)(1+theta_b^(i))+x_((i-1)b+1)y_((i-1)b+1)(1+theta_(b+1)^(i))+...+x_(ib)y_(ib)(1+theta_2^(i))](1+delta_i), with |theta_j^(i)|<=bar_gamma_j and |delta_i|<=tilde_u_FMA. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.2)]
For i=1, because s_0=0, the theta index multiplying x_1y_1 is b rather than b+1. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: sentence following equation (3.3)]

There exist alpha_k and beta_k for k=1,...,n such that hat_s_n=sum_(k=1)^n x_k y_k(1+alpha_k)(1+beta_k), |alpha_k|<=tilde_gamma_q^FMA, and |beta_k|<=bar_gamma_n. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: compact factorization preceding equation (3.4)]
The absolute forward error satisfies |s_n-hat_s_n|<=(tilde_gamma_q^FMA+bar_gamma_n+tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n)|x|^T|y|. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)]
If (3.1) is evaluated from right to left, every occurrence of bar_gamma_n in the bound may be replaced by bar_gamma_(q+b-1). [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.4)]
Without the right-to-left sharpening, the bound displayed in (3.4) remains valid for every order of evaluation of (3.1). [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.4)]
definitions_and_conventions: The exact scalar is s_n=x^T y=sum_(k=1)^n x_k y_k; a hat denotes the computed value. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1) and equation (3.4)]
Absolute value is componentwise, so |x|^T|y|=sum_(k=1)^n |x_k||y_k|. [PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: componentwise absolute-value convention; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)]
For a unit roundoff v, gamma_k(v)=kv/(1-kv). Thus bar_gamma_k=k bar_u/(1-k bar_u), and tilde_gamma_k^FMA=k tilde_u_FMA/(1-k tilde_u_FMA). [PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: gamma notation]

The effective precision is defined by the prioritized cases tilde_u_FMA=u if u>u_FMA; otherwise tilde_u_FMA=0 if bar_u>=u_FMA; otherwise tilde_u_FMA=u_FMA if bar_u<u_FMA. [PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3) and its following precedence sentence]

A mixed-precision block FMA takes blocks A in R^{b1 x b}, B in R^{b x b2}, and C in R^{b1 x b2}; A and B are supplied in u_low, while C and the returned block may use u_low or u_high. [PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: mixed-precision block-FMA definition]
implicit_context: The scalar result is the entrywise analysis of one row-column dot product arising inside Algorithm 3.1; applying it to every row-column pair yields a matrix-product analysis. [PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: opening of section 3.2]

Algorithm 3.1 first replaces inputs by tilde_A=fl_low(A) and tilde_B=fl_low(B) if necessary. Equation (3.4) analyzes the chained dot-product arithmetic itself, while the sentence following (3.4) limits its direct application to inputs already given in u_low. statement.algorithm_linkage: Algorithm 3.1 initializes each output block C_ij to zero and performs q updates C_ij=C_ij+tilde_A_(i,l)tilde_B_(l,j) using block FMAs. contract_plain_english: For one length-n row-column dot product, split the n products into q=n/b consecutive blocks and accumulate those blocks from zero as in Algorithm 3.1. Under the standard relative-error model, the gamma-validity conditions, the authors' prioritized effective-rounding definition, and the exclusion of underflow and overflow, the computed full result admits per-product factors bounded by tilde_gamma_q^FMA and bar_gamma_n. Therefore its absolute forward error is at most (tilde_gamma_q^FMA+bar_gamma_n+tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n)|x|^T|y|, with componentwise absolute values and with no first-order truncation. Right-to-left evaluation permits bar_gamma_n to be replaced by bar_gamma_(q+b-1), while the original bound is claimed for every evaluation order. Initial input-conversion error and the second rounding in the stated double-rounding case are not included in this local bound.
